meta-description: Amazon Interview Experience – Round 3 (LLD Round) 🚀

Round 3 at Amazon  for SDE2(L5) was a Low Level Design (LLD) interview, and it was a deep dive into how you think, not just what you code.

🔗: https://lnkd.in/g--NmUZc

The primary problem discussed was designing Splitwise. The discussion covered:
	•	Designing core entities (User, Group, Expense, Transaction)
	•	Maintaining and updating user balance sheets
	•	Handling different expense types (equal, exact, percentage)
	•	Validating balances and ensuring correctness of calculations
	•	Discussing algorithms to keep balances minimal and consistent
	•	Trade-offs, edge cases, and extensibility of the design

What stood out in this round was the focus on clarity of thought:
	•	How cleanly you model real-world problems
	•	How well you justify design decisions
	•	How you evolve the design step by step instead of jumping to code

Want to get interview calls from these top companies and prepare well for them , checkout these
🔗 https://lnkd.in/g--NmUZc
🔗 https://lnkd.in/ghgfxPPz

The interviewer was less interested in perfect syntax and more interested in:
✔️ Object modeling
✔️ Responsibility separation
✔️ Correctness & scalability
✔️ Communication of ideas

This round reinforced one key lesson for me:

Good LLD is about simplifying complexity while keeping the system flexible for future changes.

Hope this helps anyone preparing for Amazon / FAANG LLD rounds.

Happy to share resources and preparation tips—feel free to comment or DM 🙌
